analysis.title: GS Pasi - What's Trending Across Credit 4 Oct 2026
key_insights: Credit is trading apart from equities. The S&P finished roughly flat and Nasdaq made new highs, while rate vol stayed elevated, European sovereign risk returned, HY decompressed sharply and the Paramount Skydance (PSKY) financing struggled in secondary.

Higher yields no longer reliably support credit. Earlier this year higher yields slowed opportunistic issuance and drew in yield buyers. Recently, higher rates have coincided with wider spreads as total returns turn negative and MOVE stays elevated.

IG widened only about 2bps on the week, but the index yield crossed 6% for the first time since 2023 and long corporates reached about 6.6%. IG is roughly -3% YTD on total return despite historically tight spreads, and IG funds saw about $2.3bn of outflows.

IG primary passed a stress test with some indigestion. About $37bn priced across eight deals, mostly the ~$30bn PSKY first-lien financing. Oversubscription averaged ~2.3x vs ~3.9x YTD and new-issue concessions rose, which the author reads as investors becoming more price sensitive rather than the market being closed.

PSKY set the tone in secondary. The 10y IG tranche finished roughly +17bps wider than pricing and the ~$12.4bn second-lien HY tranches (8y/10y) ended the week about 4pts below issue after trading as much as ~6pts lower. The weakness spilled into BB and high-beta credit.

The IG supply outlook turns supportive. September issuance was about $217bn and Q4 is estimated at only ~$330bn versus $684bn/$635bn/$546bn in Q1/Q2/Q3, with net issuance potentially close to flat. With IG yields above 6% and defensive positioning, the author is more constructive on the medium-term technical if rates stabilize.

French fiscal and political concerns pushed 10y OAT yields about 62bps higher over the past month, with the OAT/Bund gap at levels last seen around the European sovereign crisis. French Yankee benchmarks widened roughly 20-30bps vs ~5-10bps for German and UK peers, and Italian financials have begun to catch up.

EUR financial credit underperformed across the capital structure this week: Senior Non-Preferred ~16bps wider, Tier 2 ~22bps and AT1 ~55bps. EUR IG has widened ~20bps over the past month vs roughly flat USD IG, one of the clearest regional dislocations in credit.

Fixed income is where the volatility is showing up. US bond ETFs reached as much as 27% of total ETF volumes, roughly 2x the longer-run average, and US fixed income ETFs are approaching $500bn of net inflows YTD despite negative returns in broad bond indices.

September was a heavy HY month. About $51bn of issuance was the second-busiest September on record, and SoftBank and PSKY were the two largest HY deals ever. SoftBank was absorbed cleanly while PSKY was not, which shows strong order books do not guarantee secondary demand at current valuations.

Decompression moved beyond CCCs. HY cash widened ~12bps vs ~2bps in IG, CDX HY widened ~16bps vs ~2bps in CDX IG, and BB spreads widened ~22bps on the week. September was the worst monthly HY return since September 2022, driven by higher rates, about $2bn of fund outflows and heavy supply into very tight starting valuations.

Loans look better placed than fixed-rate HY. Loans are about +3% YTD vs negative returns in HY and IG, backed by ~$96bn of excess measurable demand over net supply through September and the coming repayment of WBD's ~$15bn TLB. Higher-quality loans still slipped 0.125-0.25pt this week and ETF redemptions accelerated.

Sector dispersion in leveraged finance is large. Software has recovered because feared AI disruption has not shown up in earnings and maturities were pushed out. Building Products fell ~5% in September and ~10% YTD on housing, rates and inflation. Software is ~11% of the loan market vs <1% for Building Products.

Insurance brokers remain a pressure point. The HY insurance broker index widened roughly 75bps over the past week. Acrisure's 6.75% 32s fell another ~5.5pts with the rest of its capital structure down ~2-3pts on leverage concerns, and Asurion's 32s/34s fell ~2pts.

Equities have not reflected the stress seen in credit, rates, oil and sentiment. SPX is within ~1% of its highs, Nasdaq set another record and VIX is in the mid-teens. HYG implied vol relative to equity vol reached a multi-year extreme, and the desk frames the outcome as either credit and rates stabilizing toward equities or equities eventually acknowledging tighter financial conditions.

Positioning is already defensive. Fundamental equity L/S net leverage fell for three straight weeks to ~46%, near five-year lows, and non-dealers sold ~$68bn of SPX futures over six weeks. In credit, hedge funds flipped between HY shorts, HY roll longs and protection, then covered CDX shorts after Friday's softer payrolls while real money kept adding risk.

Rates may be finding their own constraint. European sovereign stress pulled Bund yields lower and interrupted the duration selloff, and softer US labor data and more dovish Fed/ECB communication helped. Higher yields are contributing to the financial tightening that can limit how far yields rise.

HY/IG decompression is described as the cleanest macro-credit theme. Real money buys weakness while macro accounts hedge through HY, leaving HY rich to NAV into Friday's rally. With macro uncertainty high, index products and vol are seen as a more active way to express risk than outright IG cash.

ETFs amplified activity but did not cause the HY selloff. PT inquiry was ~$39bn, 1.8x the recent run rate, HY ETF flows were ~1.9:1 better for sale, ETFs still took in ~$1.6bn from 9/25-10/1 and HYG never closed at a discount to NAV. Cash led the weakness.

Global credit spreads have moved toward quarter-end forecasts. Year-end targets remain modestly tighter, partly on the usual late-December supply slowdown, but GIR sees room for more volatility through early December if rates stay unstable. French sovereign risk is expected to pass through mainly via financials.

French fiscal and political concerns are lifting the OAT/Bund gap to crisis-era levels and passing into French and European financial credit.

trade_ideas.description: Hedge further European sovereign weakness through financial credit, and selectively add risk where the selloff created value

risk_factors: Total returns on IG and HY are negative YTD and elevated MOVE is weakening yield-based demand for credit.
French fiscal and political stress could keep widening OAT/Bund and spread into European financial credit, with no fresh catalyst to reverse it.
Large primary deals such as PSKY may keep failing in secondary, signaling price-sensitive demand.
Equities could eventually reprice for tighter financial conditions given the divergence from credit, rates and oil.
Insurance broker leverage concerns (Acrisure, Asurion) and sector pressure in Building Products.
HY and loan fund outflows and ETF redemptions are accelerating.
Rates may stay unstable, leaving room for more spread volatility through early December.
vol_and_positioning: HYG implied volatility relative to VIX reached a three-year extreme, while VIX remains in the mid-teens and SPX is within ~1% of its highs.
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell to the 2nd percentile on a five-year lookback, about 46% net, and monetary policy optimism is near historical lows.
Non-dealers sold about $68bn of SPX futures over the last six weeks.
Investors have broadened macro hedging into IWM downside, HYG/TLT convexity and single-stock protection, as equity performance concentrates in AI/TMT.
Hedge funds added HY shorts and IG downside early in the week, moved to HY roll longs, then returned to protection as spreads widened, and covered CDX shorts after the softer payroll print.
HY was rich to NAV into Friday's rally even as the roll curve bear-steepened earlier in the week.
geopolitical: French fiscal and political concerns are pushing OAT yields higher and widening the OAT/Bund differential to levels last seen around the European sovereign crisis, with BTP/Bund following.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is already defensive, all-in IG yields are above 6%, Q4 IG gross supply is expected near ~$330bn vs $546bn in Q3, and equities are holding near highs with Nasdaq at records. The desk is more constructive on the medium-term IG technical.
tension_points.bear_case: IG is about -3% YTD on total return, HY had its worst month since September 2022, EUR financials are under sovereign stress, and HYG implied vol vs VIX is at a three-year extreme. Equities may eventually reprice to tighter financial conditions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rates failing to find a range, with higher yields continuing to coincide with wider spreads and negative total returns.

tension_points.bull_case: OAT/Bund screens wide to fundamental measures, and sovereign stress pulled Bund yields lower and interrupted the duration selloff, which helps duration.
tension_points.bear_case: Without a fresh catalyst to reverse French fiscal concerns, the stress keeps passing through French and European financials and EUR IG.

theme_stances.key_argument: Credit, rates, oil and sentiment show stress while SPX stays within ~1% of its highs, so either macro assets stabilize toward equities or equities catch down.
theme_stances.evidence: The divergence itself has become increasingly difficult to ignore

theme_stances.key_argument: With IG yields above 6%, defensive positioning and much lighter Q4 supply, the medium-term technical improves if rates stabilize.
theme_stances.evidence: I am becoming more constructive on the medium-term technical

theme_stances.key_argument: French OAT widening transmits into EUR financial credit, with AT1, Tier 2 and Senior Non-Preferred bearing the brunt.
